title: NBI files complaints vs 13 over smuggled cigarettes

 Cebu Gothongs deny probe 
 DAVAO. Arnel Pura, outgoing director of the NBI Cebu District Office. Photo by April Blanche Cabanog April Blanche Cabañog Published on :  Nov 10, 2026, 7:20 am 
 Copied 
 Summary The NBI filed DOJ complaints on Nov. 9, 2026, against 13 individuals—including Gothong family members—over the alleged P13 billion cigarette smuggling under Republic Act 12022.
 Carlos A. Gothong Lines Inc. stated it has not received formal notice of the complaints, maintaining it unwittingly transported sealed containers as a domestic common carrier.
 Gothong Southern Shipping Lines Inc. clarified that it is not currently the subject of any investigation regarding the 59 confiscated containers in Mandaue City.
 THE National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has filed complaints against 13 individuals, including Gothong family members, over the alleged smuggling of P13 billion worth of cigarettes. Meanwhile, Gothong Southern Shipping Lines Inc. (GSSLI) denied being under investigation and Carlos A. Gothong Lines Inc. (Cagli) stated it had not received formal notice of the complaints.
 The complaints were filed with the Department of Justice (DOJ) on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, for alleged violations of Republic Act 12022, or the Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act.
 Arnel Pura, outgoing director of the NBI Cebu District Office, said the complaints were jointly filed by the bureau’s Cebu and Manila offices following an investigation into the shipments.
 NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the offenses carry severe penalties, including life imprisonment and may be nonbailable under the law.
 “As disclosed by our director, Atty. Melvin Matibag, the case was already referred for prosecution for violation of agricultural smuggling, a non-bailable offense, against those named personalities,” Pura said.
 Among the respondents are two employees assigned to the Gothong office and another worker at the company yard, Pura confirmed.
 He did not provide the complete list of the 13 respondents or identify the specific Gothong office involved.
 Pura said the Bureau of Customs (BOC) has requested that the 59 confiscated containers be transferred to its port area to reduce the burden on personnel assigned to secure the shipments.
 The DOJ will evaluate the complaints and supporting evidence to determine whether they warrant preliminary investigation and, ultimately, the filing of criminal charges in court.
 Under the DOJ’s rules, prosecutors must determine whether the evidence establishes a prima facie case with reasonable certainty of conviction before charges can proceed to court.
 Alleged facilitator identified 
 Investigators identified a respondent allegedly responsible for arranging the transportation of the 59 containers to the Gothong Wharf in Mandaue City, where the shipments remain under BOC security.
 Pura identified the individual as Veralyo, who allegedly coordinated with a trucking company to transport the shipments.
 He clarified that the trucking company owner’s affidavit did not, by itself, establish the respondents’ involvement. However, investigators found that Veralyo had arranged the transportation on behalf of the still-unidentified owner of the goods.
 “The trucking company was merely conducting its regular business operations. Based on our investigation, Veralyo was the one who made the arrangements and acted as the facilitator on behalf of the still-unidentified owner of the goods,” Pura said.
 Two Chinese nationals were also named as respondents after investigators examined consignee registration records obtained from the Department of Trade and Industry and the Bureau of Internal Revenue.
 Authorities have yet to determine whether the registered consignees represent legitimate businesses or fictitious entities.
 Pura said NBI agents in Cebu handled the confiscation of the containers, gathered witness affidavits and submitted supporting documents.
 Gothongs deny being under investigation 
 Cagli, which operates as Gothong Shipping and maintains an office at GT Ferry Wharf in Mandaue City, said it had no knowledge of the contents of the containers linked to the alleged smuggling case. GSSLI, meanwhile, maintained that it was not under investigation.
 In separate statements, the two shipping companies addressed reports concerning the alleged smuggling of foreign cigarettes and the filing of complaints with the DOJ.
 Cagli said it had not formally received any legal documents or official notice regarding the reported case filing.
 The company maintained that, as a domestic common carrier, it transports cargo based on declarations made by shippers and does not handle customs clearance or the verification of import duties.
 Shipper-sealed containers 
 Cagli explained that the containers involved were shipper-owned containers (SOCs), which are handled under the maritime industry’s standard “Shipper’s Load and Count” (SL&C) arrangement.
 Under this arrangement, the shipper is responsible for loading, counting and sealing the cargo before handing the containers over to the carrier.
 The company said the containers were already sealed when it received them, leaving its personnel, according to the company, without the opportunity or authority to inspect or verify their contents.
 “In this arrangement, we have no knowledge as to the character of the goods sealed inside,” Cagli said.
 It maintained that its personnel had neither the opportunity nor the right to inspect the cargo inside the sealed containers.
 “As a common carrier acting in reliance on the shipper’s declarations, our company is also an unwitting victim of these circumstances,” it added.
 Domestic cargo operations 
 Cagli also emphasized that its operations are limited to transporting cargo within the Philippines and that it does not engage in international shipping.
 The company said cargo accepted for domestic coastwise transport is presumed to have undergone the necessary customs clearance before being turned over to domestic carriers.
 “Consequently, border control and the verification of tax and customs duty payments fall entirely outside our mandate and concern as a domestic carrier,” it said.
 Cagli maintained that verifying whether import taxes and customs duties had been paid was outside its responsibilities as a domestic carrier.
 The company said it would respond to any allegations once it receives the appropriate legal documents.
 “Once we receive the proper legal documentation, we will fully address and answer all allegations in accordance with the due process required by law,” it said.
 Gothong Southern clarification 
 Separately, GSSLI denied that it was under investigation in connection with the alleged transportation of smuggled foreign cigarettes.
 “In light of recent reports concerning the transportation of foreign cigarettes in alleged violation of customs regulations, Gothong Southern wishes to clarify that it is not currently the subject of any investigation in connection with this matter,” the company said.
 It added that it respects due process and the authorities’ responsibility to establish the facts.
 Gothong Southern emphasized its commitment to lawful trade practices and responsible cargo handling as a common carrier.
 “We will continue to strengthen our processes and work closely with our people, shippers and partners to uphold the integrity of the cargo entrusted to us,” it said.
 Both companies reaffirmed their commitment to lawful shipping operations and cooperation with authorities. / ABC, MVG
